title: GePBench: Evaluating Fundamental Geometric Perception for Multimodal Large Language Models
claim: The benchmark spans six distinct fundamental perception task types, each illustrated by a simple shape image with a multiple-choice question.
layout: 6 cards in 3x2 grid, each with image left, question right
description: A 3-row by 2-column grid of rounded, cream-yellow cards with gold borders. Each card shows one task aspect: Counting, Reference, Existence, Location, Size, and Relationship. The aspect name appears in bold at top left. Beneath it is a dashed-border square containing a black line drawing of geometric shapes such as triangles, circles, ellipses, spirals, hexagons and rectangles. To the right is a bold 'Question:' heading, a natural-language question, four lettered multiple-choice options in two columns, and a bold 'Answer:' with the correct option. Examples include counting triangles, finding the absent shape, and asking whether a hexagon is circumscribed about a circle. The look is uniform and monochrome apart from the cream cards. The eye is drawn to the shape drawings and bold headings.

abstract: Geometric shapes play important roles in both physical world and human cognition. While multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have made significant advancements in visual understanding, their abilities to recognize geometric shapes and their spatial relationships, which we term \emph{geometric perception}, are not explicitly and systematically explored. To address this gap, we introduce GePBench, a novel benchmark specifically designed to assess the geometric perception capabilities of MLLMs. Our extensive evaluations reveal that even the current state-of-the-art MLLMs exhibit significant deficiencies in geometric perception tasks. Furthermore, we show that models trained with GePBench data demonstrate considerable improvements on a wide range of downstream tasks, highlighting the critical role of geometric perception in enabling advanced multimodal applications. Our code and datasets are available at \href{https://github.com/Changhao-Xiang/GePBench}{https://github.com/Changhao-Xiang/GePBench}.
